# Sirach Chapter 36 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_036_page_001.jpg

---

36:1 Have mercy on us, O Lord God of all, and look upon us,

36:2 and send your dread upon all the nations.

36:3 Lift your hand against foreign peoples and let them witness your power.

36:4 As you have been shown holy in us before them, so be magnified in them before our eyes;

36:5 and may they acknowledge you just as we have acknowledged you, that there is no God but you, O Lord.

36:6 Repeat your signs and work new wonders; make your hand and right arm glorious.

36:7 Stir up your wrath and pour out fury; destroy the adversary and wipe out the enemy.

36:8 Hasten the end and remember your sworn oath, so that people will recount your mighty acts.

36:9 Let fiery wrath consume what remains, and let those who abuse your people meet their destruction.

36:10 Crush the heads of hostile rulers who say, "There is no one but ourselves."

36:11 Assemble all the tribes of Jacob and restore them to their inheritance as in former times.

36:12 Show mercy, O Lord, to the people who are called by your name, Israel, whom you called your firstborn.

36:13 Have compassion on your holy city, Jerusalem, the place where you rest.

36:14 Fill Zion with the proclamation of your deeds, and your temple with your glory.

36:15 Bear witness on behalf of those you created at the beginning, and bring to pass the prophecies spoken in your name.

36:16 Reward those who wait for you, and let your prophets prove trustworthy.

36:17 Hear the prayer of your servants, in accordance with the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all who live on the earth may know that you are the Lord, the eternal God.

36:18 The belly will accept every kind of food, but one food is better than another.

36:19 The palate tells the difference between game, and a discerning mind detects false words.

36:20 A devious heart causes grief; but a person of experience can pay back in kind.

36:21 A woman will accept any man, but one woman is better than another.

36:22 A woman's beauty makes a man's face light up; there is nothing so desirable as this.

36:23 If in addition there is kindness, meekness, and gentleness on her tongue, her husband is not like other men.

36:24 Whoever acquires a wife has his finest possession, a helper suited to him and a column of support.

36:25 Where there is no hedge, the property is stripped bare; and where there is no wife, a man wanders about sighing.

36:26 Who trusts an agile robber that darts from city to city? So too, who trusts a man who has no home and stays wherever evening overtakes him?
